name: Buybacks

subjectOf.text: Stewardship pressures push companies toward an unhealthy focus on short-term dividends and share buybacks designed to please the stock market, the opposite of the long-term orientation the codes intend.
subjectOf.abstract: Indeed, stewardship pressures often expose companies to an unhealthy focus on short-term dividends and share buybacks designed to please the stock market.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, The ‘Unmediated’ and ‘Tech-Driven’ Corporate Governance of Today's Winning Companies (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2922176
scope_conditions: companies subject to institutional investor stewardship pressure

subjectOf.text: A focus on dividends and share buybacks makes it extremely difficult for a company to fund the innovation investment on which long-term relevancy depends.
subjectOf.abstract: Figure 2 illustrates that a focus on dividends and share buybacks makes it extremely difficult for a company to invest in innovations that are critical to maintaining relevancy
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, The ‘Unmediated’ and ‘Tech-Driven’ Corporate Governance of Today's Winning Companies (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2922176
scope_conditions: S&P 500 companies, 2012 to 2016 revenue growth data

subjectOf.text: Ten of the thirteen S&P 500 companies with above-average revenue growth over the 2012 to 2016 period had never paid a dividend and had never engaged in share buybacks.
subjectOf.abstract: Figure 2 shows that ten out of the thirteen S&P 500 with an above-average revenue growth have never paid any dividends to their shareholders and were never engaged in share buyback activities.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, The ‘Unmediated’ and ‘Tech-Driven’ Corporate Governance of Today's Winning Companies (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2922176
scope_conditions: thirteen S&P 500 companies with above-average revenue growth, 2012 to 2016
